significance: The treaty took Egypt out of the Arab-Israeli military conflict; Egypt was expelled from the Arab League.

headline: Soviets vote in first contested elections
summary: On 26 March 1989 Soviet voters went to the polls for the Congress of People's Deputies, the first contested national elections since 1917.
significance: Many party officials were defeated and Boris Yeltsin won a Moscow seat by a landslide.

headline: TV Marti begins broadcasting to Cuba
summary: On 27 March 1990 the US government's TV Marti began test broadcasts to Cuba from a balloon tethered in the Florida Keys; Cuba jammed it.
significance: The station was part of the US propaganda effort against Castro; Havana called it electronic aggression.

headline: Three Mile Island nuclear accident
summary: On 28 March 1979 a reactor at the Three Mile Island plant near Harrisburg, Pennsylvania, suffered a partial meltdown.
significance: It was the worst accident in US commercial nuclear history and stalled American nuclear construction.

headline: Nuclear trigger smuggling sting at Heathrow
summary: On 28 March 1990 British customs and US agents seized capacitors destined for Iraq at Heathrow Airport after an eighteen-month sting, saying they could be used as nuclear-weapon triggers.
significance: Baghdad denied any nuclear purpose. The seizure exposed Iraqi procurement networks months before the invasion of Kuwait.

headline: Airey Neave killed by car bomb at Westminster
summary: On 30 March 1979 Airey Neave, Conservative spokesman on Northern Ireland and a wartime escaper and intelligence officer, was killed by a car bomb at the House of Commons.
significance: The INLA claimed the killing. Neave had been a close adviser to Margaret Thatcher.

headline: Reagan shot in assassination attempt
summary: On 30 March 1981 President Reagan was shot and wounded outside the Washington Hilton by John Hinckley Jr.
significance: Reagan recovered quickly, and his popularity rose.

headline: Georgia votes for independence
summary: On 31 March 1991 Georgians voted overwhelmingly in a referendum to restore the country's independence.
significance: Georgia declared independence on 9 April 1991, the anniversary of the 1989 Tbilisi massacre.

headline: Warsaw Pact military structure dissolved
summary: On 31 March 1991 the Warsaw Pact's military structures were formally dissolved, following a decision of its members in February.
significance: The alliance itself was dissolved on 1 July 1991, leaving NATO as Europe's only military bloc.

headline: UN imposes sanctions on Libya over Lockerbie
summary: On 31 March 1992 the UN Security Council adopted Resolution 748, imposing an air and arms embargo on Libya for failing to hand over the Lockerbie bombing suspects.
significance: The two suspects were alleged Libyan intelligence officers. The sanctions remained until their surrender in 1999.
